title: Fermy Lab – Portfolio | Studio 1947
description: Brand identity, packaging and omnichannel UI for Fermy Lab — a fermented food brand bridging traditional Indian culinary wisdom with modern design.
ogDescription: Brand identity, packaging design, and omnichannel UI system for Fermy Lab — an innovative fermented food brand bridging traditional Indian culinary wisdom with modern design.

hero.alt: Fermy Lab horizontal logo lockup — the wordmark in deep green and golden ochre above a row of ingredient icons

body: When food founders and consumer brands look for a creative agency, they aren't just looking for attractive graphics. They want to see a functional commercial system — one that establishes immediate credibility on a grocery shelf, commands attention on digital delivery platforms, and smoothly adapts as the company scales.
This case study breaks down how we transformed the foundational values of Fermy Lab into a highly polished, scalable identity system engineered for real-world business growth.

sections.heading: Context & The Challenge
sections.label: The Mission
body: Fermy Lab is an innovative food brand that creates premium products using slow, natural fermentation methods. The brand seamlessly bridges traditional Indian culinary wisdom with time-tested techniques sourced from diverse cultures around the world. Their focus is on making food that is healthy, enjoyable, and environmentally responsible, completely refusing to rely on artificial preservation shortcuts.

sections.label: The Creative Challenge
body: The brand's core identity operates at a distinct crossroads: balancing deep tradition with modern thinking, local roots with global ideas, and natural patience with scientific rigor. To visually express this balance, we anchored the branding in a concept of “calm confidence”. The style is engineered to look systematically clean yet warm and handcrafted, proving to consumers that slow food can be professional, clean, and world-class.

sections.heading: Parent-Brand Architecture
body: To protect the client from future design costs, we built a "parent-child" visual system designed to accommodate future growth:

media.alt: Parent-brand architecture diagram — the Fermy Lab master mark sitting above two product tracks, Breads and Condiments, each with its own product line labelling

body: Fermy Lab functions as the overarching master identity. Under this umbrella, the brand launches with two distinct product tracks: Breads and Condiments. Each individual item carries its own product line labeling, while the corporate master-mark retains prominent authority across the entire ecosystem. This allows the business to launch new items instantly without paying for a total brand redesign.

sections.heading: Color & Typography Systems
sections.label: The Palette
body: The color identity relies on a high-contrast pairing designed to command attention on store shelves:

swatches.name: Deep Green
swatches.note: Represents natural fermentation cycles, organic balance, and core safety and trust.

swatches.name: Golden Ochre
swatches.note: Evokes warm oven-baked goodness, rich raw nourishment, and human-crafted culinary expertise.

cards.title: Space Grotesk
cards.body:
Usage
Structural Headlines, Packaging Titles, and Technical System Signage.

The Strategy
Space Grotesk introduces a clean, disciplined geometric frame that reinforces the empirical, “Lab” aspect of the brand name. It maintains flawless sharpness across physical print packaging and digital screens. Because it is freely accessible in the open-source Google Font library, internal marketing teams can build matching assets globally without licensing friction.

cards.title: Just Sans
cards.body:
Usage
Narrative Brand Copy, Back-of-Label Explanations, and Detailed Ingredient Lists.

The Strategy
To balance the technical look of the primary font, we paired it with Just Sans. This typeface introduces an endearing, modernist warmth and geometric legibility. It ensures that health labels and brand stories remain highly approachable and effortless for consumers to scan.

sections.heading: The Logo Usage & Visual Governance
body: To ensure perfect consistency across entirely different physical labels and screen environments, all configurations, safety guidelines, and visual prohibitions are unified into a single technical standard.

media.alt: Overview of the Fermy Lab logo usage system — the approved lockup configurations gathered into one technical standard

sections.label: The Master Badge Lockup
body: This layout serves as the primary seal of quality, beautifully integrating the brand name, core product ingredients, and service taglines into a circular stamp. It features an organic, illustrative wreath highlighting real ingredients: twisted challah bread, garlic bulbs, star anise, cloves, and chilis.

media.alt: The master badge lockup — a circular Fermy Lab stamp ringed by an illustrated wreath of challah bread, garlic, star anise, cloves and chilis

sections.label: The Horizontal Lockup
body: Created specifically to guarantee high visibility within tight spatial restrictions, this inline variation seats the core wordmark directly above a streamlined row of ingredient icons.

media.alt: The horizontal lockup — the Fermy Lab wordmark set inline above a streamlined row of ingredient icons for tight spaces

sections.label: Responsive Favicons
body: Simplified, high-contrast circular badges that isolate a single key icon, such as the mini bread loaf or an organic clove, keeping the identity sharp on micro-screens.

media.alt: Responsive favicon set — simplified circular badges each isolating one icon, such as the bread loaf or a clove, for micro-screen legibility

sections.label: The 1-Challah Clearspace Rule
body: To protect the mastermark from being crowded by copy or layout borders, it must always be insulated by a minimum safety border. This breathing room is defined as exactly equal to a "1 Challah distance," derived from the height of the internal twisted bread illustration.

media.alt: Clearspace diagram — the master badge surrounded by a minimum safety border measured as one challah loaf height on every side

sections.label: Partner Co-Branding Safety Margin
body: When co-branding alongside external distribution partners or legacy institutions—such as locking up next to historic entities like Amul—the system enforces a strict 1-Challah safety perimeter to protect FermyLab's independent authority.
The FermyLab logo isn't just a symbol, it's a statement. Keep it clear, crisp, and confidently placed.

media.alt: Co-branding diagram — the Fermy Lab mark locked up beside a partner logo with the mandated 1-Challah safety perimeter between them

sections.heading: Absolute Production Prohibitions
body: To eliminate any guesswork for third-party printers or internal developers, we codified an explicit checklist of system violations. Production environments are strictly prohibited from making the following adjustments:

media.alt: Violation matrix — a checklist of prohibited treatments of the Fermy Lab mark, such as recolouring, stretching and rotating it

sections.label: Delivery App Optimization
body: The brand assets were optimized for dark-mode smartphone delivery interfaces. This ensures that when a consumer is quickly scrolling through restaurant choices, FermyLab’s product cards, metadata, and icons remain perfectly crisp and legible.

media.alt: Delivery app listings — Fermy Lab product cards, metadata and icons tuned for dark-mode smartphone food-delivery interfaces

sections.heading: Commercial Value Summary
body: By delivering a disciplined, complete brand utility rather than loose, disconnected graphic files, we equipped Fermy Lab with a high-performance system tool. The business is fully prepared to stand out on physical shelves, command digital interfaces, and launch entirely new sub-brands with absolute operational confidence and zero added design debt.
